The president of Cornell University is breaking his silence,
saying the school must do better
amid criticism of its handling of rape allegations.
In a video released on Saturday,
Michael Kotlikoff acknowledged frustration
over how little Cornell has said publicly about its response.
There are real legal and privacy limits

Guns, immigration, and climate change are on the docket
as the U.S. Supreme Court opens a new term on Monday.
Among the many controversies facing the court
is a question that the justices have long avoided,
namely whether it's unconstitutional
to ban semi-automatic assault-style weapons.
NPR's Nina Totenberg reports.
On the one hand, for instance, the AR-15 rifle
can deliver up to 100 bullets per minute
without any enhancements.
On the other hand, there are some 16 million
semi-automatic weapons in the U.S.,
and it's unclear, for instance, how a ban would work
without taking weapons away from law-abiding citizens.
There are many other controversies facing the court,
everything from test cases on public funding
for religious schools,
lengthy detention of immigrants without a hearing,
and of course, very likely,
questions about the conduct of elections.
Nina Totenberg, NPR News, Washington.
Voters in Brazil go to the polls today.
The country's incumbent left-wing president
is locked in a tight contest with the son of his rival,
the former far-right president
convicted of staging a coup.
NPR's Carrie Khan has more.
Both say the contest is too close to call
between veteran leftists Luis Anacio Lula da Silva
and Flavio Bolsonaro, a current senator.
Lula, now 80, is facing a tough re-election
with voters concerned about crime,
corruption, and a faltering economy.
Bolsonaro says if he wins, he will align more closely
with President Trump's anti-drug interventionist policies
in the region.
While Trump has not publicly endorsed Bolsonaro,
he says he's watching the contest closely
and touts his clout in the region,
which has seen the last seven presidential contests
shift to right-wing leaders that align with the U.S.
Lula says he's willing to work with Trump as partners
but insist on respect for sovereignty.
Carrie Khan, NPR News, Rio de Janeiro.
- You're listening to NPR News from Washington.

as the state reviews Wednesday's failed execution

Governor Bill Lee announced the departure

Pike's lawyers say she's unconscious

The U.S. Coast Guard says crews have found a debris field
from a missing Canadian air ambulance
off Nantucket, Massachusetts.
The plane was carrying six people from Bermuda to Boston
when it disappeared early yesterday morning.
The search continues for the aircraft.
Many churches this weekend are holding
their annual blessing of the animals.
NPR's Jason DeRose reports it's an opportunity
for people of faith to bring along their pets to worship.
- In recent decades, congregations have welcomed pets
not just into the parking lot for the annual blessing

- Almighty Father, we bless these animals
for all they have done for us.
- The blessing usually takes place on or near
the feast of St. Francis of Assisi,
the patron saint of animals and the environment.
Among the stories told about Francis
is one in which he preached to birds,
telling them they too were loved by God.
(birds chirping)
The blessing of the animals comes at the end
of the new ecumenical season of creation
that many churches are marking for the first time this year.
Jason DeRose, NPR News.
- I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News in Washington.
